doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: WPA block dances in the street
summary: Depression-era WPA hired seven-piece bands to play pop tunes for dancing in roped-off streets, which Bucky watched as a boy.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: You mentioned some street dances they would do.

Yeah. And during the Depression the WPA and the NRA — National Reconstruction Association or something like that, and the other one was the Works Progress Administration — would hire musicians to play block dances on your street. There weren’t many cars in those days. So they would block off the middle of the block, rope it off, and have seven musicians play for dancing in the street.
And they would be playing what kind of music?
Which was what at the time?
Well whatever, “The Music Goes Round and Round,” [sings] and it comes out — and whatever the big bands were playing they would play.
That’s neat. Were you a dancer?
No, no. I was only a little kid in those days.
I’d stand behind the ropes and watch. Watch the band more than anybody else.
